title: Replace legacy statsd + log-shim with evented observability gateway
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Our in-service telemetry path still routes many low-cardinality metrics and structured logs through a legacy synchronous statsd adapter and a log-shim that serializes events inline. This path contributes to observable tail-latency spikes during traffic bursts, increases CPU consumption on hot hosts, and makes sampling inconsistent across spans, metrics, and logs. Goal: Replace the legacy sync path with an evented observability gateway (EOG) that: 1) accepts instrumented envelopes (span/metric/log) asynchronously, 2) performs bounded-batch aggregation and async export to configured exporters (OTLP/Prometheus/Cloud), 3) centralizes sampling decisions so traces/metrics/logs can be correlated, and 4) exposes a compatibility shim for existing internal statsd and log-shim clients during rollout. Success metrics: - Reduce telemetry-induced p99 tail latency on runtime hotpaths by >=60% under burst load (measured on microbench harness) - Reduce median CPU consumed by telemetry hotpath by >=25% - End-to-end telemetry correlation (trace_id present on metric events for 95% of sampled traces) - No customer-facing metric loss after compatibility window rollout (backfill plan validated) Work breakdown: - Spike (done): prototype EOG process that receives protobuf envelopes over unix socket, implements bounded queue + worker pool, and exports to a local OTEL collector. Measured baseline: prototype drops <0.1% at 10k eps with 4 worker threads and 32ms tail latency. - Implementation: production-grade EOG written in Rust (for low allocation), with feature-flagged compatibility shim that translates statsd counters to envelope metrics and attaches tracing context when present. - Sampler harmonization: move sampling decision into EOG policy engine; provide config to respect existing client-side flags for incremental rollout. - Exporter plugin system: adapters for OTLP (gRPC), Prometheus remote write (push gateway), and our existing parcel forwarder. - Observability & QA: end-to-end tests, fuzzing for malformed envelopes, load/stress harness, and dashboarding for queue depth, export success, latency breakdown. - Rollout plan: deploy EOG as sidecar on canary hosts behind feature flag -> enable shim translation -> flip ingestion to EOG for a small tenant -> monitor for 72h -> progressive ramp across regions. Compatibility notes: - The shim will accept hot-code config so we can toggle sampling modes without requiring host restarts. - Backfill: for the first 48 hours after flip, the EOG will snapshot and forward translated legacy metrics to a backfill topic to ensure dashboards remain consistent. Acceptance criteria: - EOG binary passes internal performance CI (latency + CPU) and integration tests - Feature-flagged rollout completes for one internal tenant with no missing metrics > 1% - Security review sign-off for RPC surface and KMS access for any exporter credentials - PRs reviewed and merged: runtime changes, shim client updates, console metric mapping docs Rollback criteria: - Telemetry drop >1% sustained for 30 minutes - Runtime p99 telemetry-induced latency increase >20% vs baseline - Unrecoverable exporter errors after retries (exceeding rejection threshold)
